title: DMT keeps oxygen-deprived neurons alive via the sigma-1 receptor
summary: Andrew Gallimore tells of DMT keeps oxygen-deprived neurons alive via the sigma-1 receptor, about recent at unspecified laboratory, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: >> Um what's interesting is that in a oxygen hypoxic oxygend deprived environment um neurons will survive longer in the presence of DMT.

plain: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that nerve cells starved of oxygen survive longer when DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound, is present. As the story's title frames it, this happens through the sigma-1 receptor, a protein on cells that DMT can attach to. If true, it would suggest the brain's own DMT may help protect it when oxygen runs short.
